definition: Training an AI agent within a simulated environment rather than the real world, allowing for faster, cheaper, and safer iteration.
details: Simulation-based training is widely used in robotics and reinforcement learning research, since it allows generating vast amounts of experience quickly and safely testing behaviors that would be risky or costly in the real world.

explainer.lead: Simulation-based training lets an agent learn inside a simulated world instead of the real one. It makes iteration faster, cheaper and safer, which is why it dominates robotics and reinforcement learning research.

tiers.eli5: Like practising driving in a simulator so you can crash a hundred times without anyone getting hurt.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers generate large amounts of experience in simulation and test risky behaviours there first. The pitfall is that simulated experience may not carry over to the real world without further transfer work.
tiers.paperLevel: Training occurs against a simulated environment that approximates the target task; the method is defined by that substitution rather than by a specific algorithm.

explainer.example: A reinforcement learning agent practises a grasping task thousands of times in simulation before any real robot is involved.
